newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Dresdner braces for wave of consolidation.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dresdner braces for wave of consolidation.

text.p: Dresdner Bank AG said on Tuesday it will fill its war chest for a possible purchase in the U.S. and forge closer ties with insurer Allianz AG to reinforce its position in a sector hellbent on consolidation.

The moves come amid a massive realignment in Germany's financial services industry signalled by last week's news of a merger between two Bavarian banks that will topple Dresdner from its position as Germany's Number Two bank.

The increased cooperation with Allianz also points to the polarisation of the sector between two competing giants -- Allianz and Deutsche Bank AG -- as insurers and banks battle for the growing market for asset management.

Dresdner said it will increase its base capital by 120 million marks ($65.3 million) through a rights issue with one new share being offered for every 20 held. The subscription period runs from August 14 to August 28.

The bank said the move would boost its equity capital by more than 1.2 billion marks to over 16 billion marks and "broaden its scope for strategic moves" -- a statement that came as red rag to a bull in a stockmarket brimming with merger speculation.
The capital increase would establish a "war chest" for purchases abroad, chief executive Juergen Sarrazin told the bank's half-year news conference.

Dresdner was focusing on the U.S. in its search for a possible acquisition to broaden its base in the investment banking sector, Sarrazin said. But the bank was not in talks and had not identified a partner yet.
Analysts expect the proceeds from the capital increase to total 1.7 to 1.9 billion marks -- less than the one billion pounds Dresdner spent to take over UK investment bank Kleinwort Benson in 1995.
Dresdner's equity capital will rise to more than 17 billion marks by end-1997 following the expiry of a warrant bond.
A purchase would mark the continuation of a vigorous and costly expansion drive into foreign investment banking in recent years.

Sarrazin denied the capital increase was a reaction to the planned fusion between Bayerische Vereinsbank AG and Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG -- a merger sanctioned by Allianz, which will own roughly 16 percent of the merged group.

Like market leader Deutsche Bank AG, Sarrazin sought to play down the emergence of the powerful new Munich-based banking force, saying it would affect competition within Germany but have little impact on Dresdner's growing global business.

"We are not completely different, but we are different," he said. "International orientation has a special significance at Dresdner. We regard ourselves as a global player in various areas such as asset management."
The growing market for asset management is one area in which Dresdner plans to cooperate more closely with Allianz.

The two, which are linked through sizeable cross shareholdings, already sell each other's respective banking and insurance products and also plan to cooperate more in property finance. Sarrazin said the closer link with Allianz was a "decisive factor in our strategic thinking."
Allianz owns roughly 22 percent of Dresdner while Dresdner holds 10 percent of Allianz.

Analysts had predicted Dresdner and Allianz would seek to work together more closely and some expect Dresdner to join forces eventually with the Bavarian group, to be called Bayerische Hypo- und Vereinsbank AG.
Merger speculation has completely overshadowed a glowing set of first-half results which has set up Germany's top five banks for record earnings this year.
Dresdner reported a 23 percent rise in earnings in the first half of 1997, confirming a trend of rising earnings boosted by this year's steep stock market rally.
Dresdner said its operating profit rose to 1.74 billion marks from 1.42 billion in the year earlier, just above analysts' average expectations of a rise to 1.67 billion marks.
Also on Tuesday, Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG (Hypo-Bank), Germany's fifth largest bank, said operating profit rose 17.2 percent to 651.7 million marks.
The result was slightly below analysts' expectations for an operating profit figure of 686.5 million marks.
Separately, Dresdner said it had been picked to lead manage the flotation of the German government's remaining stake in airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG.
($ = 1.836 German Marks)
